capacity.label: Licensed capacity, children
capacity.assumption: A mid-sized center for the trade area. Directory capacities for Gonzales-area centers run from small home-scale programs to several well above this level, but those figures carry no date, so the study prints none; the Ready Start Network counts 28 early learning centers in the parish [^12]. The state license fee schedule also steps up at 101 children [^22].

occ.label: Enrolled children as a share of licensed capacity
occ.assumption: Ramps over three years to 84%, then 88%. No competitor occupancy was found and the research holds no utilization figure for the parish, so the path is an underwriting choice: demand is strong (the parish added several thousand residents between April 2020 and July 2025 [^4]) but the center must still take children from established programs, and a 150-child center opens with every classroom empty. The sensitivity table moves occupancy 20% either way.

share_young.label: Share of enrolled children under age 3
share_young.assumption: Infant and toddler rooms are the costliest to staff and the most scarce; the mix is a planning choice, not a market statistic.

share_pre.label: Share of enrolled children ages 3 to 5
share_pre.assumption: The largest group, as at most centers; this share also includes pre-kindergarten children.

share_school.label: Share of enrolled children in school-age before and after care
share_school.assumption: Competitors in the census run before and after school care and summer camp for primary-school children [^14,15]. The subject carries a smaller school-age program than a center beside a primary school would.

rate_young.label: Weekly tuition, under age 3
rate_young.assumption: Inside the range of weekly rates by age that the Dutchtown center publishes on its own site [^14]. The study does not print the competitor's posted rates, because the research dates them only by a check, not by a publication. Infant care is the highest-priced room.

rate_pre.label: Weekly tuition, ages 3 to 5
rate_pre.assumption: Inside the same posted range, at the preschool end; three- to five-year-olds are the lowest-priced full-time rooms.

rate_school.label: Weekly rate, school-age before and after care
rate_school.assumption: Inside the range of before- and after-school rates the same operator publishes [^14]; school-age children attend part of the day, so the weekly rate is far below a full-time rate.

weeks.label: Billed weeks per year
weeks.assumption: Fifty-two weeks less closed holidays; a center bills across the summer, so there is no seasonal gap beyond a few unbilled days.

tuition_index.label: Tuition level against the modelled schedule
tuition_index.assumption: A multiplier on all three weekly rates, held at 1.00 so that the sensitivity table can move tuition up and down.

tuition_growth.label: Annual tuition increase
tuition_growth.assumption: A planning rate close to general inflation; the research holds no Gonzales tuition history, so no local increase is claimed.

fees_per_child.label: Registration, supply and late fees per enrolled child per year
fees_per_child.assumption: Operators in the census charge a one-time registration fee per child [^14]. This is an allowance for registration, annual supply fees and late-pickup charges; the research states no Gonzales total.

cpt_young.label: Children per teaching post, under age 3
cpt_young.assumption: A blended classroom ratio for infant, toddler and two-year-old rooms. The licensing ratios are in the state's center rules, which the research cited for fees and license types, not ratios [^22]; the lender should replace this figure with the rule's.

cpt_pre.label: Children per teaching post, ages 3 to 5
cpt_pre.assumption: A blended preschool ratio, an assumption pending the same check against the state rule.

cpt_school.label: Children per teaching post, school-age
cpt_school.assumption: School-age groups run at the loosest ratio; an assumption pending the same check.

paid_hours.label: Paid hours per teaching post per year
paid_hours.assumption: A center open from early morning to evening staggers shifts so that ratios hold through the middle of the day and thin at its edges; the model pays one full-time equivalent, 2,080 hours, for each classroom post. Competitors in the census run a long day with before and after care [^14,15].

wage_teacher.label: Average hourly wage, teaching staff
wage_teacher.assumption: The midpoint of the $13.00 to $15.00 hourly range a Geismar center advertised for a toddler assistant in August 2025 [^17]. Most teaching posts are assistants, and the few leads earn more, so the midpoint stands for the blend. The advertised range is a single posting, not a market survey.

admin_payroll.label: Director, assistant director, cook and office payroll, Year 1
admin_payroll.assumption: A director, an assistant director, a cook and part-time office help; the research holds no Gonzales salary for any of them. It is the largest non-classroom cost and a lender condition to price from a payroll quote.

burden.label: Payroll taxes, workers' compensation and benefits on wages
burden.assumption: Employer taxes and workers' compensation for a labour-intensive service business; no Louisiana child care figure was found.

inflation.label: Annual growth in wages and operating costs
inflation.assumption: A planning rate; the research states no Louisiana inflation figure, so none is claimed.

food_per_child.label: Meals and snacks per enrolled child per year
food_per_child.assumption: An allowance. Centers that accept subsidy children often serve meals, and the research found no Gonzales food cost; a lender should ask for the center's food program.

supplies_per_child.label: Curriculum, supplies and consumables per enrolled child per year
supplies_per_child.assumption: An allowance; no Gonzales supply cost was found.

utilities_psf.label: Utilities per square foot of building per year
utilities_psf.assumption: An allowance for electricity, water, sewer, gas and telephone for a building that runs long hours. Whether water, sewer and electric service reach a site is a lender condition, and the utility providers were not found.

insurance.label: Property, liability and abuse-and-molestation insurance, Year 1
insurance.assumption: An allowance; no Ascension Parish premium was found, and the lender should obtain quotes.

repairs_psf.label: Repairs, janitorial and grounds per square foot of building per year
repairs_psf.assumption: An allowance for a building with heavy daily use.

admin.label: Licenses, accounting, software, marketing and parent communications, Year 1
admin.assumption: An allowance. The state's annual license fee for a center of this size is $250 and the application fee is $25 [^22]; the balance is accounting, parent software and advertising.

tax_rate.label: Property tax as a share of cost basis
tax_rate.assumption: The research found only undated millage tables and no commercial assessment ratio, so no rate is printed from them; this is a round 1.2% allowance for a commercial parcel outside the city's boundaries, and the parcel's actual taxing districts are a lender condition.

reserve_pct.label: Replacement reserve, share of furniture, equipment and playground cost per year
reserve_pct.assumption: Funds classroom furniture, kitchen equipment and playground surfacing over a roughly twelve-year cycle.

land_acres.label: Land area, acres
land_acres.assumption: A round hypothetical parcel of about two acres, enough for a building of this size, a drop-off lane, parking and a fenced outdoor play area.

land_per_acre.label: Land cost per acre
land_per_acre.assumption: A round planning figure for commercial land on a growing corridor. The research found no closed land sale in Gonzales; it did find two commercial parcels of about this size offered for sale in the town during 2025 and 2026, and the model's figure sits between their per-acre asking prices. Asking prices are not sales, so the appraisal and an executed contract replace it. The sensitivity of the verdict to land is small beside enrolment and tuition.

building_sf.label: Building size, square feet
building_sf.assumption: About 80 square feet of building per licensed child, for classrooms, a kitchen, offices, bathrooms and circulation. For scale, a 7,400 sq ft center in Dutchtown changed hands in April 2025 [^13]; this building is considerably larger because it carries 150 children.

building_psf.label: Building hard cost per square foot
building_psf.assumption: A planning allowance. The research lists a construction cost index for the parish as not found and holds no Gonzales bid. For scale, the 7,400 sq ft Dutchtown center sold with its land for $860,000 in April 2025 [^13]; that is a used building, so new construction is carried well above it.

sitework.label: Site work: paving, drainage, utility taps, fencing and signage
sitework.assumption: An allowance for a two-acre parcel with a drop-off lane and parking. Parish impact and connection fees were not found [^20], so they are a lender condition.

playground.label: Outdoor play areas: shade structures, surfacing and equipment
playground.assumption: An allowance for age-separated play areas.

contingency_pct.label: Hard-cost contingency
contingency_pct.assumption: Five percent of building, site work and play areas, a planning choice for a priced but unbid project.

soft.label: Design, permits, survey, Phase I environmental, legal and state approvals
soft.assumption: An allowance. A new center needs parish zoning approval, fire marshal and public health approvals and a certificate of occupancy before the state will license it [^33]; new or renovated space also needs approvals before occupancy [^23].

ffe.label: Furniture, kitchen, security, technology and a vehicle
ffe.assumption: An allowance for classroom furniture and cribs, a commercial kitchen, door security and cameras, a parent check-in system and one van.

working_capital.label: Pre-opening payroll, licensing carry and operating reserve
working_capital.assumption: A planning reserve for pre-opening payroll, licensing carry and the Year 1 operating loss while the center is licensed and fills; a state license can take weeks after construction ends, and the center earns nothing until then.

uses.label: Building, 12,000 sq ft
uses.basis: sq ft x cost per sq ft

uses.label: Design, permits, Phase I and legal

revenue.label: Tuition, under age 3
revenue.expr: capacity * occ * share_young * rate_young * weeks * tuition_index * (1 + tuition_growth) ** y
revenue.basis: children x weekly rate x weeks

revenue.label: Tuition, ages 3 to 5
revenue.expr: capacity * occ * share_pre * rate_pre * weeks * tuition_index * (1 + tuition_growth) ** y
revenue.basis: children x weekly rate x weeks

revenue.label: School-age before and after care
revenue.expr: capacity * occ * share_school * rate_school * weeks * tuition_index * (1 + tuition_growth) ** y
revenue.basis: children x weekly rate x weeks

opex.label: Teaching payroll
opex.expr: capacity * occ * (share_young / cpt_young + share_pre / cpt_pre + share_school / cpt_school) * paid_hours * wage_teacher * (1 + inflation) ** y

opex.label: Property tax
opex.expr: (land_acres * land_per_acre + building_sf * building_psf + sitework + playground + ffe) * tax_rate

proposed.note: the sponsor proposes the program's start-up minimum of 10% equity

breakeven.label: enrolment as a share of licensed capacity
